classification.difficultyReason: Combine the conditional-probability definition with the explicitly cued independence product rule, then cancel the positive denominator to establish the identity.

content.prompt:
[Proving the independence condition]

Suppose $A$ and $B$ are independent events and $P(B)>0$. By considering the formula for $P(A\cap B)$ when $A$ and $B$ are independent events, prove that $P(A\mid B)=P(A)$.

answer.short: $P(A\mid B)=P(A)$. Use $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$ in the conditional-probability formula.
answer.worked:
Independence gives $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$. Since $P(B)>0$,

$$\begin{align*}P(A\mid B)&=\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}\\P(A\mid B)&=\frac{P(A)P(B)}{P(B)}\\P(A\mid B)&=P(A).\end{align*}$$
